text.p: Pay television operator Australis Media Ltd said on Wednesday net subscriber disconnects for the period December 1, 1996 to January 31, 1997 were 1,000 net disconnects and are currently the lowest level in over a year.
Australis said from March 1996 to November 30, 1996 it suffered an increase in the level of net subscriber disconnects, which it does not believe would continue in the future.

"The company has substantially arrested the decrease in its own subscriber base and achieved a customer base which it believes will not be subject to the high level of subscriber disconnects previously sustained," Australis said.

Australis said it expects the current action taken against rival pay TV network, Foxtel to be resolved soon. The action relates to an underpayment of revenue due of about US$3.85 million, which was earned substantially in the December half.
It said its subscriber numbers totalled 97,000 at January 31, while franchisee subscribers totalled 129,000 and Foxtel subscribers were 140,000.
Australis and Foxtel have a programming sharing arrangement.
It said Foxtel subscriber numbers are expected to improve as Telstra Corp, which owns 50 percent of Foxtel, continues to pass more homes in its A$3.0 billion cable rollout prgramme.

"Any sustained slowdown in this (Telstra) rollout or the penetrations achieved by Foxtel will be monitored by the company as these are an important source of revenue for the company and in the event there is no material improvement this may lead to a revision in the company's estimate of its cashflow breakeven position during mid-1998," Australis said.
Australis reported a net loss of A$103.6 million in the six months ended December 31, 1996. Last year, the group reported a net loss of A$97.50 million in the 1995/96 half.
Australis shares ended one cent lower at 15 cents.
